Papercusp Project History is a generated, versioned read model plus a reusable interactive renderer for product-facing History pages. It is reusable across projects: the installed CLI reads the selected Papercusp harness and Git repository, the pure `@papercusp/plan-parser` assembler produces schema v2, `@papercusp/ui-primitives` renders the shared History behavior, and each app supplies only a thin transport and styling adapter.

## Generate an artifact

Run from the consumer repository:

```bash
papercusp project-history generate \
  --harness my-project \
  --prefix= \
  --project-id my-project \
  --project-name "My Project" \
  --repo . \
  --output .papercusp/project-history.v2.json
```

The default plan filter is `<harness>-`; `--prefix=` deliberately disables it and exports the complete harness. Use `--workspace` when the process does not already carry `PAPERCUSP_WORKSPACE`. Repository origin, GitHub web URL, and default branch are detected from Git and may be overridden explicitly.

JSON is the portable default. For a server package that wants a build-time import, add `--format typescript --export-name PROJECT_HISTORY`; this changes transport only, not schema. Add the identical command with `--check` to a focused build/test gate. Check mode compares deterministic output and fails without rewriting when the committed artifact is stale.

## Validation-aware schema v2

Every plan item carries `validationAssertions`, parsed from its canonical inline `VAL-*` blocks. Each assertion preserves the plan item id, verification command or condition, evidence locator, status (`todo`, `validating`, `passed`, or `failed`), whether a test is required, and the canonical source line. Each plan also carries a `validationSummary` roll-up with total, status, and test-required counts.

Consumers must reject unknown `schemaVersion` values. Missing, incomplete, failed, and stale validation stay explicit; raw validator logs do not become timeline entries. Proof remains attached to the plan item or completed work item it validates.

## Authority and provenance

The artifact is disposable derived output. Plan/work-item ledgers, `git_sync_commit_attribution`, and Git remain authoritative. Completion tree stamps describe what was verified before git-sync and are never treated as landed commits. Commit links retain attribution (`authoritative`, `body-reference`, or `inferred`) and remote status (`confirmed`, `local-only`, or `unknown`). A browser URL is emitted only when repository web identity is known.

Bulk work-item reads use the file-backed `work_items:export` path. Omitting its `limit` means a complete export; an explicit cap reports `truncatedByLimit` and Project History refuses partial output. This keeps evidence-rich ledger rows off the bounded model-result transport without silently losing old completions.

## Shared consumer contract

Render schema v2 with `ProjectHistoryView` from `@papercusp/ui-primitives`. The shared component owns search and filters, delivery summaries, validation proof, expandable work-item and commit details, plan dialogs, pagination, and accessibility semantics. Product adapters may supply transport, labels/actions, class/slot styling, and theme tokens, but must not fork schema interpretation or interaction behavior.

Papercusp exposes the shared surface at **More → History** for the active project/harness through `GET /api/harness/:slug/project-history`. SideStage remains the first external consumer and supplies only its product adapter.

## Installed packaging

Desktop builds ship `sidecar/scripts/project-history.mjs` as a narrow self-contained bundle and route it through `~/.papercusp/bin/papercusp` and the Debian `/usr/bin/papercusp` twin. Consumers invoke the bare installed command; they never require `PAPERCUSP_REPO_ROOT` or a Papercusp source checkout. The bundle uses the shared ESM `HOST_BANNER` because yaml's CommonJS dynamic require otherwise fails only after packaging.

## Template onboarding

Compose `papercusp-project-history`. Its GUIDE carries the decision points and its portable `project-history-artifact` check validates schema v2, project id, harness, generator, plan-count integrity, per-plan validation summaries, and per-item assertion arrays.

## Verification checklist

1. `papercusp project-history help` works from the installed dispatcher.
2. Generate once, then rerun the same command with `--check`.
3. Run the portable aspect check with `TEMPLATE_CHECKS_CONFIG`.
4. Run the shared UI, consumer adapter, API route, navigation, and accessibility tests.
5. Verify the rendered page against the generated artifact; no live database read belongs in the consumer app.
6. Confirm an explicit capped export fails closed when `truncatedByLimit` is true, while the default file export completes beyond normal list limits.
